newsitem.title: USA: Ammonia leak likely cause of fire at Excel plant.
newsitem.headline: Ammonia leak likely cause of fire at Excel plant.

text.p: An ammonia leak in a freezer unit was the likely cause of an explosion and fire that severely damaged the loading dock area at Excel Corp's Ottumwa, Iowa pork plant, company and fire officials said.
"It looks like there was an ammonia leak that caused the explosion that led to a fire," said Mark Klein, Excel spokesman.

The plant is closed this week and no date has been set for reopening. Hourly workers have begun signing up for unemployment benefits, Klein said. The plant has about 1,300 employees and about 1,000 are hourly workers, Klein said.
No official damage estimates have been released but fire officials said it could be in "the millions."
"The roof is completely gone at the loading dock," said Ottumwa Fire Department Captain Zilba Backus. "They will have to completely rebuild it."
Excel's Klein said customer orders continue to be filled and Ottumwa's pork production has been shifted to Excel plants in Marshall, Mo., and Beardstown, Ill.
The 20-year-old Ottumwa plant can slaughter 9,600 hogs a day, but is being expanded to slaughter 15,000 head daily.
Excel Corp is a unit of Cargill Inc.
